issues.technical: fill_pdf (representative.py:225-297) never calls authorize_action or log_action. Reproduced with paperwork at 'recommend': the certify checkbox /Yes, Signed and vault:signature were written; 0 action-log entries. egress.jsonl does record the call with its values.
issues.fix: Detect signature fields (/Sig, vault:signature, sign/certify/attest wording, attestation checkboxes) and require authorize_action('paperwork', ...) before writing them, then log_action; refuse if not at 'act'.

issues.title: Driver's licence and passport numbers are stored in the profile and released to plain guest sessions
issues.plain_words: JEFFEREY accepts your driver's licence and passport numbers as ordinary profile details and gives them to any plain Claude or ChatGPT session. These are the numbers identity thieves want.
issues.technical: SENSITIVE_PATTERNS (representative.py:57-63) lacks licence/license, passport, maiden name, place of birth and security question. Reproduced: set_profile_field stored both; claude-raw get_profile returned them. Health cards are already refused, fill_form did not auto-fill the licence, and the maiden-name issue is the mapping bug in I-30.
issues.fix: Add licence/license, passport, maiden name, place of birth and security question to SENSITIVE_PATTERNS so they are vault-only, and withhold non-form identifiers from guest keys.

issues.title: ChatGPT server token hygiene: weak and duplicate tokens accepted, no lockout or failure log, docs open
issues.plain_words: If the ChatGPT connection is set up with a short or repeated password, JEFFEREY accepts it without warning, and a one-letter password was guessed in 11 tries. Failed attempts aren't recorded or blocked, and the server's own documentation pages are open to anyone.
issues.technical: JEFFEREY_HTTP_TOKENS is never checked for length or duplicates (jefferey_http.py:89-102; last duplicate wins, so the family app got the jefferey key). Scheme match is case-sensitive (:125). 401s are not logged, there is no lockout, and /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc return 200 with no token. The docstring example uses 's3cr3t' and recommends a tunnel (:22-23, 89). The single-token default is token_urlsafe(24) (:79).
issues.fix: Refuse tokens under 32 characters and duplicates at startup; parse the scheme case-insensitively; log 401s with source IP and back off after N failures; disable docs/redoc/openapi when exposed; use generated tokens in the docstring.

issues.title: Prompts accept only single letters: typing 'shut' doesn't shut the door, and 'no' renames the drive or keeps a recording
issues.plain_words: In 'What left the house', typing 'shut' or 'stop' opens the log instead of shutting the door, and nothing says the door is still open. In other prompts, typing 'no' renames your drive or keeps a voice recording as consent.
issues.technical: What left the house.command:33-39 matches only s|S, and the default branch pages the log. Make-drive launcher lines 66-71 skip renaming only on n|N. voice_enrol.py:262-289: 'skip' and 'quit' start the mic, and 'no' at the keep prompt keeps the take as consent. Reproduced on byte-identical copies of the launchers.
issues.fix: Normalise answers (lowercase, first word) and accept shut/stop/close/ferme, open/ouvre, y/yes/oui, n/no/non, s/skip/passer, q/quit. Re-ask on anything unrecognised. Require an explicit yes to rename and to keep a consent take. Always print the door state after acting.

issues.title: Photo folders dragged in from Finder aren't un-escaped, so 'Show me my life' exits on any folder with a space
issues.plain_words: Dragging your 'Family Photos' folder into the window, which is what most people do, makes 'Show me my life' say there's nothing there and quit. Pressing return instead may index the Photos library's internal copies or another Mac's pictures.
issues.technical: go.py:101 strips only quotes and whitespace and go.py:105-107 calls sys.exit(1) after one wrong answer. photo_index.walk (photo_index.py:272-289) descends into .photoslibrary bundles (6 files for one photo). The make-drive launcher un-escapes '\ ' only (line 47) and asks again.
issues.fix: Use shlex.split when the input has backslashes, strip, and keep asking until the folder exists. Skip *.photoslibrary and bundle dirs in walk() and explain how to export originals.

issues.title: The memory file and its backups are created readable by every account on the Mac
issues.plain_words: JEFFEREY's memory file and its backups are saved so that any user account on the Mac can read them, unlike its log, which is private. Other people's accounts on a shared Mac can open your life story.
issues.technical: conscience.py:341-342 creates the tmp file with open(tmp,'w') under the umask; snapshots use mkdir/write_bytes (311-316). Observed with umask 022: dir 0755, conscience.json 0644, history 0755, snapshots 0644; the lock and egress.jsonl are 0600.
issues.fix: os.umask(0o077) at each surface's start; create tmp files with O_CREAT|O_NOFOLLOW mode 0600, history/namespace dirs 0700, snapshots 0600; chmod existing ~/.jefferey on startup.

issues.title: Renaming the drive breaks every indexed photo path
issues.plain_words: If the drive's name changes, for example from 'Self Cloud' to 'Self-Cloud' during setup, every photo on the wall stops showing. Re-scanning doesn't repair it.
issues.technical: Stored paths are absolute; cmd_build and scan_once (photo_index.py:439-442) never update a known sha at a new path, and scan_once on the old path returns early. Reproduced: after os.rename, stored paths all missing, scans returned (0,0,0,0), wall.thumbnail None; renaming back restored it.
issues.fix: When a known sha appears at a new path with its stored path missing, update path and clear missing_since; better, store paths relative to the drive root and re-root at read time.

issues.title: Access refusals reach Claude as a bare 'Error executing tool X', so first-run key mistakes look like crashes
issues.plain_words: When JEFFEREY refuses Claude something because of its key, Claude only sees 'Error executing tool', so it looks broken rather than protected. A typo in the key name looks like a crash too.
issues.technical: egress.through (egress.py:573-582) converts only EgressRefused; AccessDenied/OwnerOnly from @gate propagate, and mcp 2.3.0 (tools/base.py:211-213, mcpserver/exceptions.py:61-67) reduces them to 'Error executing tool <name>'. Reproduced in a real stdio session (who_am_i/remember_fact as claude-raw; JEFFEREY_CLIENT=claude_raw).
issues.fix: Catch AccessDenied and OwnerOnly in jefferey_mcp.door and return the same {refused, reason, tell_the_user} as dispatch_tool (or raise ToolError). Validate --client against the presets in install.py.

issues.title: Make-drive launcher: tracebacks on unwritable drives, endless loop on closed input, rename with no answer, installer disk images offered
issues.plain_words: The drive-setup window can rename a work drive without anyone answering, list a software installer as a drive choice, or crash with a technical error on a Windows-formatted drive. People unfamiliar with computers won't know what went wrong.
issues.technical: Reproduced on a launcher copy with /Volumes replaced: closed stdin chose --rename on 'Work Archive'; a read-only 'Claude' DMG was listed and answering 1 gave OSError [Errno 30] with misleading next-step text; EOF loops; no icon without a logo. provision() does not catch OSError around mkdir/write.
issues.fix: Catch OSError in provision() with a plain refusal and check writability first; branch on status before hints; use `read -r ... || exit 1`; exclude read-only and installer volumes; require an explicit yes to rename.

issues.title: Variant SIN labels (NAS, S.I.N., tooltips, generic names) are not recognised as sensitive
issues.plain_words: A form box labelled 'NAS' or 'S.I.N.' isn't recognised as asking for your SIN, so JEFFEREY tells the AI to ask you for it in chat. A SIN written with dots can also be put into such a box.
issues.technical: Sensitive-field detection is label-substring only (representative.py:397-425) and doesn't normalise punctuation or read /TU; _SIN accepts only space or dash (egress.py:217). Reproduced: only 'SIN' mapped to the vault; '046.454.286' written under 'S.I.N.'. Impact check refuted most of the harm: admit() refuses spaced, dashed and plain SINs whatever the label, and a literal SIN reaching fill_pdf means the owner already typed it to the AI.
issues.fix: Normalise labels (strip punctuation, add NAS and 'numéro d'assurance sociale', read /TU). Strip all non-digits before the Luhn/SIN checks. Refuse any literal that passes a SIN or card check in fill_pdf.

issues.title: Egress log short writes count as success: data leaves while its log entry is torn
issues.plain_words: On a full drive, JEFFEREY can hand data to the AI while its log entry is only half written. The next entry is then lost too, so 'What left the house' misses both.
issues.technical: egress._write does not loop on short os.write and does not check for a trailing newline. Reproduced on a real 128 KB tmpfs: get_conscience released 6,083 chars with a 4,096-byte torn log; the next send left 1 parseable and 1 unparseable line. system_prompt_once marks the prompt announced even on failure.
issues.fix: Record size, loop os.write until done, and on a short write or error ftruncate back and refuse the send; add a newline if the file doesn't end with one; set _ANNOUNCED_SYSTEM only after a successful write.

issues.title: A damaged memory shows up as a failed self-test at install and as a silent disconnect in Claude
issues.plain_words: If the memory file is damaged, the installer says JEFFEREY's self-test failed, as if the program were broken, and Claude just shows it as disconnected. The repair instructions are buried in the last lines of a technical trace.
issues.technical: install.selftest imports jefferey_chat, whose Conscience() at import (jefferey_chat.py:51) raises ConscienceCorrupt on the real store, although selftest itself uses a temp store (1494-1497). The MCP server dies on start.
issues.fix: Run the selftest with a temp JEFFEREY_CONSCIENCE_PATH or create the store lazily; add a separate 'Your memories: OK / recovered / need restoring' line; on ConscienceCorrupt start a degraded MCP server with one tool that explains the restore.

issues.title: Claude Code wiring is local-scope only
issues.plain_words: The installer says it connected JEFFEREY to Claude Code, but it only works inside the JEFFEREY folder. Opening Claude Code anywhere else shows no JEFFEREY.
issues.technical: install.py:199-202 runs 'claude mcp add' without --scope (default local). Reproduced with Claude Code 2.1.296: 'Scope: Local config' in the repo, 'No MCP server named jefferey' elsewhere.
issues.fix: Pass --scope user to the add and remove calls, including in unwire().
